title: Slow Cooker Beef Stew
cook: 8 hr on low or 4 hr on high
total: 8 hr 40 min on low (4 hr 40 min on high)

items: 3 lb boneless beef chuck roast, cut into 1½-inch cubes
1 cup dry red wine (or 1 more cup broth plus 1 Tbsp red wine vinegar)
1 lb carrots, peeled and cut into 1½-inch chunks

steps: Toss the beef with the flour, salt and pepper until coated. The flour helps it brown and thickens the stew later.

Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Sear the beef in batches, 2 min per side, adding oil as needed. Don't crowd the pan, or the meat steams instead of browning. Move each batch to the slow cooker.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the onion in the same skillet 3 min, then add the tomato paste and stir 1 min, until it darkens from red to brick.
Pour in the wine and scrape the bottom hard with a wooden spoon. Simmer 3–4 min, until reduced by half, then pour it all into the slow cooker.
Add the broth, Worcestershire, thyme and bay leaves. Set the carrots and potatoes on top, where they steam instead of sitting submerged.
Cover and cook on low 8 hr or high 4 hr without lifting the lid, until the beef is fork-tender. If it's still tough, it's undercooked; give it 45–60 min more.
Stir in the peas for the last 10 min. Remove the thyme stems and bay leaves, then taste and add salt.
tips: Buy a chuck roast and cube it yourself. Packaged stew meat is mixed scraps that cook unevenly.
Cut the carrots and potatoes at least 1½ inches. Smaller pieces break down and turn the stew pasty. Yukon golds hold their shape; red potatoes work too.

Too thin? Whisk 2 Tbsp cornstarch into ¼ cup cold water, stir it in and cook uncovered on high 15 min. Too thick? Add hot broth ½ cup at a time. Tastes flat? Add salt first, then 1 tsp red wine vinegar.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Freezer up to 3 months; the potatoes get a little grainy. Reheat covered over medium-low heat, stirring, until bubbling, with a splash of broth if it's thick.
